decisions.reason: The rejection correctly identifies that a disjoint copy of the old forcing cannot itself extend the fixed old sweetness model. Shelah's one-sided amalgamation instead requires only the first factor to extend the old model, and the inverse construction is alternated at the next stage. The exact source fact already supplied the true theorem, so the bad reconstruction was nonfatal; the proof now gives the twisted embeddings and checks the fixed first factor before taking the continuous union.

The complete proof of the dyadic supplier uses DC only in step 1.2 to derive Countable Choice; all subsequent cylinder premeasure, extension, completion, and dyadic transfer steps cite only the resulting Countable Choice interfaces. This definition assumes Countable Choice directly and expressly invokes that proof tail, so its completed coin-measure domain is licensed without assuming DC.

Clause delta did contain a genuinely free m, while the surrounding gamma and epsilon clauses and Shelah's Definition 7.7 quantify the same finite trace data over every m<n. The intended relation and the source proof were otherwise unambiguous, so this was a nonfatal binding defect. Delta now explicitly quantifies every m<n, making E_n^* a defined relation before equivalence, refinement, and sweetness are proved.

The rejection is correct that the same-real inner model theorem cannot transfer every ambient real-and-ordinal-definable set or its Baire witness upward. The item's separate source fact already cites Shelah's exact conclusion and full-extension theorem, so the equiconsistency conclusion remained supported. The proof now obtains the full-extension clause directly from that source and uses the local same-real theorem only for HOD(S).

Without a subset-of-omega domain restriction, the displayed biconditional accepts arbitrary supersets of a witnessing union, including sets containing omega itself, and therefore does not define a filter family inside P(omega). This is a fatal typing error in the public definition. The repair declares F(x) as a subset of P(omega) and quantifies the membership variable a only over subsets of omega.

The rejected restatement did overreach from a conditional external theorem about transitive set models to the ambient proper class universe. The same supplier also has the needed fixed-axiom ZF derivations of every ZFC axiom relativized to L, so the mathematical conclusion was still available. The proof now invokes that internal relativization schema inside the given ZF universe and keeps the external set-model clause out of the argument.

The rejection considered only the theorem statement, but the cited supplier's complete proof explicitly defines the admitted-pair set O, its canonical dense subset D, the least intrinsic admission modulus m(x), and the shifted factor relations E_{m+n}. Those are exactly the interfaces used by this example and by Shelah's Lemma 7.5, so the example required no mathematical edit.

The proof's error set was defined using Cohen genericity over a whole stage model, while the absorption supplier covers only meagre codes in V[s]. Dense sets of the larger model need not be V[s]-coded, so the central error containment failed. The repaired parameter algebra is generated by labelled deciding antichains; s both is read from and determines the generic trace on its countable dense algebra, proving V[G intersect C_s]=V[s]. Nongenericity witnesses are therefore exactly V[s]-coded and are absorbed by the later UM quotient.

Equiconsistency alone does not produce a forcing notion inside each supplied ZFC+CH model, so the original step could not construct the extension of N_0. The repair adds and invokes the direct CH sweet-construction theorem inside N_0, uses external countability only to build an N_0-generic ultrafilter, and then applies the separate HOD(S) theorems because N_0 was arranged to satisfy V=L.

The example incorrectly called h the first differing coordinate even though the supplier defines the first differing prefix length, which is one larger. The inequality used later was weak enough to remain true, so the defect was nonfatal. The calculation now states h(u,v)>=n+1 for a common n-bit prefix and also corrects the n=0 case from a nonexistent unique pair to all pairs.

The supplier's stated evaluation-absoluteness interface is limited to Solovay intermediate models and does not cover the Shelah HOD(S) model, so the internal Baire witnesses were unsupported. The repair proves the needed result locally: a disagreement about well-foundedness of the countable code would yield a descending real shared by both models, nodewise induction then gives identical evaluation, and the finite-cylinder characterization makes closed nowhere density arithmetic and absolute.

The complete dyadic supplier proof uses DC only to obtain Countable Choice and thereafter constructs and completes coin measure under Countable Choice. This theorem assumes Countable Choice explicitly, and its density theorem has the same hypothesis, so the uses of coin measure, independence, completion, and outer measure are all licensed. No item edit was warranted.

At beta=0 no nonzero ordinal can surject onto beta, so the claimed uniform surjection argument was false at an included endpoint. The theorem's countability conclusion is nevertheless trivial there and the positive-beta argument is valid because the chosen mu is infinite. The repair separates beta=0 and applies the constructible-choice cardinal comparison only for beta>0.

Equiconsistency with ZFC does not by itself refute the formal implication Con(all BP) to Con(ZFC plus an inaccessible), so the original refutation did not establish the claim it explicitly assigned itself. The repaired carrier states the intended and provable falsehood: an inaccessible hypothesis is not needed as an upper-bound assumption because Con(ZFC) already yields Con(all BP). It expressly disclaims the separate unproved nonimplication between bare consistency statements.

The proposed tree-code equivalence quantified every Baire real z in L[x], although binary tree bodies can contain only elements of 2^omega; the constant-two real is an immediate counterexample. That false equivalence was load-bearing for the Sigma-one-three complexity bound. The repair restricts clause (i) and every branch quantifier to binary reals while retaining the Sigma-one-two constructibility certificate and the same projective quantifier count.

The finite-prefix swaps were correctly constructed, but the displayed forcing conclusion used undeclared indices m_i and therefore did not identify them with terms of the supplier's fixed envelope. The repair names each swap rho_i, defines m_i as its least index in the canonical enumeration, and uses the exact finite range 1<=i<=k. The general absorption conclusion was already supplied independently, so this defect was nonfatal.

reviews.reason: The repaired proof now uses the twisted pair of embeddings over the target subalgebra, invokes the source's one-sided extension only for the old first factor, alternates with the inverse, and completes the order-dense union only after the continuous sweet limit. The statement and owning page remain accurate.

The measured-domain paragraph, the full dyadic supplier proof, and the completion dependencies were checked together. Countable Choice is exactly the residual hypothesis after the supplier's preliminary DC-to-CC step, so the definition and metadata remain sound and were not edited.

The five defining clauses now bind every finite trace index, with delta quantified over every active m<n exactly as in the source. Equivalence, refinement, directedness, the diagonal construction, transfer, and the separate fixed-model extension are consequently stated for a well-defined E_n^* relation.

The proof now separates the two forward models: the published source theorem directly supplies the definable-BP full extension, while the repaired HOD(S) theorem supplies ZF+DC plus universal BP only in the inner model. The reverse L argument and exact equiconsistency statement are unchanged.

F(x) is now explicitly a subfamily of P(omega), and the membership biconditional begins with a subset a of omega. This matches every later filter operation and leaves the cover and first-prefix-difference conventions unchanged. Direct consumers all use this corrected intended domain.

After DC yields Countable Choice and universal measurability yields boldface Sigma-one-three measurability, the lower-bound supplier makes ambient omega-one inaccessible in L. The final step now uses the fixed-axiom L-relativization theorem internally in V, never the supplier's conditional external transitive-set-model clause.

The complete amalgamation proof and Shelah's corresponding lemma were inspected. Both explicitly provide admitted pairs, the dense presentation, least modulus, shifted relations, complete factor embeddings, and all sweetness clauses, so the example's use is exact and its carrier stayed unchanged.

The parameter algebra is now the completion of a countable dense algebra of labelled deciding antichains, and the proof establishes V[G intersect C_s]=V[s] in both directions. Thus every failure of Cohen genericity used in the error set has a V[s]-coded closed nowhere-dense witness, exactly within the later UM absorption interface.

The proof now constructs P inside the countable ZFC+CH model using the direct sweet-construction theorem and reserves equiconsistency for the final metatheoretic comparison. The Boolean-valued quotient, same-L argument, repaired correct-omega-one lemma, Raisonnier rapidity, and nonmeasurability contradiction were rechecked in that order.

The cylinder calculation now distinguishes coordinate k from prefix length k+1 and proves the stronger bound h>=n+1. The n=0 cover is handled as the single whole-space cylinder containing every pair, and the cofinite-tail membership conclusion follows with the repaired Raisonnier filter interface.

The item now uses the Solovay supplier only for the uniform Borel-to-open construction. It independently proves well-founded-code and evaluation agreement for the transitive same-real model N, proves closed nowhere density by an arithmetic finite-cylinder test, and then uses DC to combine the actual coded error sequences inside N.

The proof was checked against the full coin-measure construction, completed density theorem, zero-one argument, rapidity estimate, and outer-measure contradiction. Countable Choice licenses every measure interface used, including the corrected F(x) domain, so no carrier or metadata edit was needed.

The proof now handles beta=0 by the empty enumeration and treats only positive beta with the constructible surjection argument. It also records why the bounding ordinal mu is infinite. Every beta below ambient omega-one is therefore counted without the impossible nonzero-to-zero surjection.

The statement and refutation now target the genuine historical claim that an inaccessible assumption is needed to obtain the relative consistency upper bound. Con(ZFC) to Con(all BP) refutes exactly that claim. The item and page both distinguish this from any unproved nonimplication between consistency statements, while preserving the measurability comparison and semantic separation.

The coded-cover equivalence now quantifies only binary constructible reals and binary branches of the tree bodies. With that type correction, the constructibility certificate is Sigma-one-two, the body and first-difference clauses have the stated projective complexity, and one existential tree-sequence code yields Sigma-one-three membership.

For the matched-width display, every full level permutation is now explicitly indexed in the canonical enumeration and the forced finite subunion has the correct one-based range. The page marks this construction as conditional, delegates general absorption to the exact supplier, and retains the unconditional singleton graft.
